chunks: The day upon which their excuses will not benefit the evil-doers, and the condemnation and evil abode will be theirs.

key_terms.سُوءُ الدَّارِ: The evil abode / bad final home

ai.seo_question: What happens to the excuses of wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Ghafir underscores the finality of divine justice, where the 'curse' (la'nah) signifies permanent exclusion from God's mercy and the 'bad abode' refers specifically to the depth of Hell. It serves as a direct counterpoint to the surah's theme of Allah's forgiveness, illustrating that while mercy is abundant, it is not available to those who persist in arrogance and wrongdoing.
